body.en:
Question B-003-019-005.

Why the correct answer is right: Filter capacitors can retain dangerous stored energy after a supply is unplugged, so they must be safely discharged before work proceeds.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Bond the chassis to ground": Chassis bonding is important, but it does not by itself remove the charge stored in high-voltage filter capacitors.
- sourceIndex 2: "Place the unit on an insulating mat": An insulating mat can be part of a safe work area, yet the capacitors may still hold hazardous voltage inside the cabinet.
- sourceIndex 3: "Short the AC input leads together": Shorting the AC input does not safely discharge the DC filter capacitors and can create a misleading or hazardous procedure.
